name: audit-4-confirm
question: On 16 fresh seeds, do Stage 3's best candidates hold up (nutrients level 2: a second feeding level and more sex; a mutation-rate floor of 0.01: bigger, steadier populations), do they work together, and does adding rare big mutations let true meat eaters take hold?

name: headline-sex
question: Does sex speed up the arrival of new feeding levels? Worlds where every animal splits in two, where sex is a gene (today's grand world), and where every animal must find a mate. An answer: when mixed eaters (5 or more) first appear and how much of the time they are present, the highest diet reached, and meat in the diet, against today's world, with 95% ranges.

name: headline-ice-age
question: Does an ice age raise or lower long-term diversity? One ice age strikes at tick 200,000 (at today's severity, 50% colder and twice as cold); diversity before it (ticks 100,000 to 200,000) and long after it (400,000 to 600,000) is compared with worlds that have no catastrophes at all. An answer: species alive and Shannon diversity after recovery against the control, with 95% ranges, and how many worlds survive each severity.

name: headline-disease
question: Does disease stop one species taking over? Worlds with no disease, with today's disease, and with a disease that infects a wider range of hosts. An answer: the share of animals in the biggest species and Shannon diversity, against today's world, with 95% ranges.

name: headline-barriers
question: Do geographic barriers produce more species? Seas covering 10%, 25% (today's) and 40% of the map. An answer: species alive and ever, Shannon diversity, and how different the animals on separate land masses are, against today's world, with 95% ranges.

name: headline-barriers-2
question: Do geographic barriers produce more species? The grand world cut into two halves by two straight water channels that animals cannot cross, against the same world uncut. An answer: species alive and ever, Shannon diversity, the share in the biggest species, and how far the two halves drift apart (the share of gene variation that lies between land masses), with 95% ranges.

name: headline-plant-quality
question: Does poorer plant food make longer food chains but fewer species, and given a million ticks, do true meat eaters (a lasting group with a diet above 0.75) take hold where plants are poor? Plant quality limits of 2 (today's), 1.5, 1 and 0.75. An answer: feeding levels, meat eaters, meat in the diet, species and population along the gradient, with 95% ranges.

name: carnivore-screen
question: What lets a lasting group of meat eaters (diet above 0.75) take hold in the grand world? A 4-seed screen of seven changes against today's grand world: diet-based mating (hunters mate with hunters), a stronger gut trade-off, richer carcasses, meat that keeps in the cold, hungry prey that defend less, weapons that get in the way of grazing, and all six together. Anything promising is confirmed on 16 fresh seeds.

name: carnivore-invasion
question: Can a ready-made group of meat eaters hold its own in the grand world once it exists? At tick 100,000 one animal in twenty becomes an armed meat eater (diet gene 0.95, attack gene 0.6; nothing else changes), and the run continues to tick 200,000. Compared: today's grand world, no sex (so mating cannot dilute them), diet-based mating, meat that keeps in the cold, hungry prey that defend less, weapons that get in the way of grazing, poorer plants (quality 1.5), and diet-based mating plus the three new settings plus poorer plants together. An answer: in which setups meat eaters (diet above 0.75) are still there at the end, and how many.

name: carnivore-invasion-big
question: Can a ready-made group of meat eaters twice the size of their prey hold its own in the grand world? As carnivore-invasion, but each invader's body is also doubled (paid from its own energy and nutrient, topped up from the soil where it stands): at tick 100,000 one animal in twenty becomes an armed meat eater twice its old size, and the run continues to tick 200,000. Setups: today's grand world, no sex, diet-based mating, meat that keeps in the cold, weapons that get in the way of grazing, poorer plants (quality 1.5), and those changes (but not no-sex) together. An answer: in which setups meat eaters (diet above 0.75) are still there at the end, against the same-size invasion.

name: carnivore-bridge
question: Why does the simple world grow meat eaters and the grand world not? Starting from the simple (default) world, each of the grand world's 15 feature groups is added alone (add-...), and the groups are also added one after another (ladder-...) until the last step is the full grand world. An answer: which group, alone or in combination, makes meat eaters (diet above 0.75, and above 0.5) disappear.

name: carnivore-bridge-2
question: Which part of the three culprits erases meat eaters, and does removing them bring meat eaters back to the grand world? Added alone to the simple world: the climate split into its parts (a temperature map only; seasons; seasons with harsh years; seasons with torpor; day and night; weather fronts; the cost of heat and cold; slow drift), sex and harmful mutations split (sex only; harmful mutations only), and kin split (kin restraint only; with herds; with sharing). Then the grand world with the culprit groups taken out. An answer: meat eaters (diet above 0.75, and above 0.5) in each.

name: gentle-culprits
question: Can the grand world keep its seasons, harmful mutations and kin restraint, only gentler, and still grow meat eaters? A 4-seed screen against today's grand world: plants swinging less with the seasons (growth swing 0.4 and 0.2, against 0.6); fewer harmful mutations (rate 1.5, against 3); more mending (0.3 and 0.5, against 0.15); tighter kin restraint (relatives only within 0.02, against 0.05); hunger overriding kin restraint (below half fed); and two combinations. An answer: meat eaters (diet above 0.75, and above 0.5), feeding levels and kills in each, and what each costs in species, sex and population. Anything promising is confirmed on 16 fresh seeds.

name: hunters-confirm
question: Does a 'hunters' grand world reliably grow meat eaters? Today's grand world against two versions without harmful mutations, sex and kin restraint: one also without the whole climate (as in carnivore-bridge-2, meat eaters in 3 of 4 worlds), one without only the seasons (keeping day and night, weather, drift, the cost of heat and cold, torpor and ice ages). 16 fresh seeds, 300,000 ticks. An answer: in how many worlds a meat-eating group (diet above 0.75) holds over the second half, how big, and what the versions cost in species and population.
